title: Some Possible Developments from a Ruy Lopez
subtitle: Imagine the structures that exchanges can produce

source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter VI, §32 Some Possible Developments from a Ruy Lopez, Example 65

steps.title: An opening that creates strategic possibilities

narration.say: We begin with the opening moves Capablanca associates with Janowski–Lasker, Paris 1912.
White challenges the centre. Black gains queenside space.
Both sides finish developing. White supports the centre and contests the e-file.
The knights manoeuvre, and White brings the queen to d3.

steps.title: A hypothetical position, not a continuous game

narration.say: Capablanca now asks us to imagine exchanges of the minor pieces. He does not give the intervening moves. The next step therefore loads a separate illustrative position.

steps.title: A backward pawn becomes a target

narration.say: The minor pieces have disappeared. Black’s c-pawn is backward, and White has active major pieces.
White brings the rook to c5. Black supports the position with c6.
The queen and second rook join the pressure.
Black’s pieces are occupied defending the queenside. White can prepare play elsewhere.

steps.title: Visualise another stage of the plan

narration.say: The book next supplies another diagram after further pawn advances. Again, the connecting moves are not given. We load the diagram rather than inventing them.

steps.title: Open a file on the other wing

narration.say: White has advanced the kingside pawns while maintaining queenside pressure. The pawn on e5 remains the strategic pivot.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Exchange the g-pawn to open the kingside.

steps.title: Move the rooks to the new battle

narration.say: White brings the queen to f3. Black returns the queen to d7.
The advanced rook returns to c2. Black shifts the rook to g6.
White brings a rook to g2. Black moves the king to h8.
The remaining c-rook joins on g1. Black answers by bringing the c-rook to g8.

steps.title: Keep the central advantage through simplification

narration.say: Queen to h5. Both pairs of rooks are exchanged on g2.
Black checks. White brings the king to h2, and the queens are exchanged.

steps.title: The pawn skeleton explains the plan

narration.say: Capablanca finishes the illustrative line with b4 and assesses the pawn ending as winning for White.
The lesson does not add a forced continuation beyond the book. White’s advanced e-pawn and the king’s freedom of movement are central to the assessment.
The opening leads to possible structures, not one compulsory future. Capablanca deliberately supplies diagrams without all the connecting moves.
Identify a weakness, tie down the defenders, and use your greater freedom to change the point of attack.
When exchanging pieces, ask whether the resulting pawn structure preserves the advantage.
